A finer-grained, peer-reviewed alternative/complement to the raw Toronto registration CSV scrapers above — gives compliance-rate framing directly (what fraction of active listings are actually registered), which is the regulator-analyst's core question and speaks to true North America STR supply versus what shows as 'compliant'.

name: Awesome-Short-Term-Rental-Operations
what_it_holds: Curated awesome-list of STR turnover/cleaning/maintenance/ops tools: commercial SaaS (Properly, Turno, Operto, Minut, Chekin, Enso Connect, Host Tools) and 4 open-source GitHub projects (tykeal/homeassistant-rental-control, Kamra-PMS/kamra-pms, Gribadan/RentTools.io, lkilpatrick/OpenSTR). No data of its own; a discovery hub. MIT license, 1 star, updated 9 Sep 2026.
why_useful: Useful map of the entire commercial STR-turnover-services landscape (confirms none of the major cleaning/turnover platforms — Turno, Properly, Operto, Minut, Chekin, Breezeway — publish open aggregate data; all are closed SaaS requiring paid per-operator accounts). Good reference if a future scout wants to re-check this space.
themes: Vacation rental damage/turnover/cleaning marketplaces (Turno, TurnoverBnB), STR supply services (Airbnb photographer, key exchange) datasets

name: Airbnb-Price-Analysis-in-Athens
what_it_holds: data/athens_weekdays.csv and data/athens_weekends.csv, split by weekday vs weekend pricing. Shape/variable naming (weekday/weekend price split for a single European city) matches the well-known Gyodi & Nawaro 'Determinants of Airbnb prices in European cities' academic dataset (originally covering Amsterdam, Athens, Barcelona, Berlin, Budapest, Lisbon, Paris, Rome, Vienna, London — ~5,000 listings/city, hedonic variables: room type, bedrooms, person capacity, superhost flag, cleanliness/guest satisfaction ratings, distance to center, restaurant/attraction indices). Repo itself is a small student analysis but the committed CSVs appear to be that dataset (or a close re-derivation) landing on GitHub, which we do not currently hold.
why_useful: If this is (or reproduces) the Gyodi-Nawaro weekday/weekend European hedonic panel, it directly fills our hedonic/mix-decomposition gap with a multi-city academic dataset that separately identifies bedroom/quality/superhost premia and a weekday-vs-weekend price wedge -- useful for ADR mix decomposition (gap 2/20) in EMEA markets outside our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel.
size_hint: 2 CSVs, likely ~5-6k rows total for Athens
time_coverage: unclear, likely a single 2018-era snapshot (matches original Gyodi/Nawaro data vintage)
themes: Airbnb and hotel price-elasticity, hedonic and mix-decomposition studies with data (bedroom counts, listing quality, superhost premium)
why_all: If this is (or reproduces) the Gyodi-Nawaro weekday/weekend European hedonic panel, it directly fills our hedonic/mix-decomposition gap with a multi-city academic dataset that separately identifies bedroom/quality/superhost premia and a weekday-vs-weekend price wedge -- useful for ADR mix decomposition (gap 2/20) in EMEA markets outside our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel.
Athens is not in our 13-city panel; adds a Mediterranean/EU geography for hedonic price-determinant comparison, though likely a single static snapshot with standard methodology.

name: Airbnb-in-Vancouver

why_useful: Vancouver is not in our current 13-city Inside Airbnb panel; this is a static full listings+calendar+reviews snapshot (likely 2019-2020 vintage based on repo age) that could extend geographic coverage for a Canada/North-America-ex-US hedonic cross-check, and the notebook is a working implementation of a named academic hedonic-pricing paper.
